text_blocks.snippet: Neutrophilic asthma is a severe, persistent form of asthma characterized by high levels of neutrophils in the lungs and airways. It is associated with frequent exacerbations, fixed airflow obstruction, and a lower FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in one second). This phenotype is often difficult to control with standard asthma treatments like inhaled corticosteroids.
